beats.title: Churchill's Iron Curtain Speech
beats.description: At a Missouri college, the former British prime minister warned that an iron curtain had descended across Europe.

beats.title: The Truman Doctrine Is Announced
beats.description: The US president pledged aid to Greece and Turkey and promised to support free peoples resisting Soviet pressure.
beats.why_in: opening Cold War crisis response in Greece

beats.title: The Berlin Airlift
beats.description: Western planes supplied a blockaded West Berlin with food and fuel for months after the Soviets cut the roads and rails.

beats.title: Germany Splits Into Two States
beats.description: The Western zones became a federal republic, and the Soviet zone answered with its own separate German state.

beats.title: The Korean War Begins
beats.description: Northern troops crossed the border into the South, drawing in a UN force led by the US and later Chinese armies.

beats.title: MacArthur Is Fired Over Korea
beats.description: The president removed his famed commander in the Far East after public clashes over widening the war into China.

beats.title: East Germans Revolt Against Rule
beats.description: Workers' strikes over higher quotas grew into nationwide protests that Soviet tanks crushed.

beats.title: The French Fall at Dien Bien Phu
beats.description: A siege in a remote Vietnamese valley ended in defeat for France and led to a country divided in two.

beats.title: Soviet Troops Leave Austria
beats.description: A treaty restored Austria's independence and neutrality, and the occupying forces of all four powers withdrew.

beats.title: The Hungarian Uprising
beats.description: Students and workers in Budapest rose against their Soviet-backed government until tanks rolled in to crush the revolt.

beats.title: The Eisenhower Doctrine
beats.description: The US promised aid and troops to Middle Eastern states threatened by communist-backed aggression.

beats.title: Khrushchev's Berlin Ultimatum
beats.description: The Soviet leader demanded the Western powers leave Berlin within six months, triggering a long standoff over the city.

beats.title: The Kitchen Debate
beats.description: A US vice president and the Soviet premier argued over rival ways of life amid a model American home at a Moscow fair.

beats.title: The Congo Crisis Erupts
beats.description: Newly independent Congo fell into mutiny and secession, with the superpowers backing rival sides.
beats.why_in: Cold War proxy conflict in Africa

beats.title: The Berlin Wall Goes Up
beats.description: East German troops sealed the border overnight with barbed wire that soon became a concrete barrier splitting a city.

beats.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis
beats.description: A thirteen-day standoff over Soviet missiles in Cuba brought the superpowers to the brink of nuclear war.

beats.title: "Ich Bin Ein Berliner"
beats.description: A US president told a vast crowd in a divided city that he stood with its people against communist pressure.

beats.title: The Gulf of Tonkin Incident
beats.description: Reported attacks on US warships off Vietnam led Congress to authorise sweeping military action in the war.

beats.title: US Combat Troops Land in Vietnam
beats.description: Marines waded ashore at Da Nang, the first major American ground force committed to the war.

beats.title: The Six-Day War
beats.description: Israel defeated Egypt, Jordan and Syria in days, in a conflict where the superpowers backed opposite sides.
beats.why_in: Cold War proxy dimension in the Middle East

beats.title: Prague Spring Is Crushed
beats.description: Warsaw Pact tanks entered Czechoslovakia to end a reform movement promising socialism with a human face.

beats.title: Soviet and Chinese Troops Clash
beats.description: Fighting on a river island on the frontier between two communist giants raised fears of a wider war.

beats.title: US Forces Enter Cambodia
beats.description: American and South Vietnamese troops crossed the border to hit enemy bases, sparking protests at home.

beats.title: The Yom Kippur War
beats.description: A surprise Arab attack on Israel became a superpower proxy war, with both sides placed on high alert.

beats.title: The Fall of Saigon
beats.description: Northern tanks rolled into the southern capital as the last Americans were evacuated by helicopter.

beats.title: The Ogaden War
beats.description: Somalia invaded Ethiopia, and the Soviet Union switched sides, backed by Cuban troops, to support Ethiopia.
beats.why_in: Cold War proxy war in Africa

beats.title: Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan
beats.description: Soviet forces poured into Afghanistan to prop up a communist government, beginning a decade of war.

beats.title: Solidarity Strikes at Gdansk
beats.description: Shipyard workers in Poland won the right to form the Eastern Bloc's first independent trade union.

beats.title: Poland Declares Martial Law
beats.description: The Polish government banned the union and arrested its leaders, under heavy pressure from Moscow.

beats.title: Soviets Shoot Down Flight KAL 007
beats.description: A Soviet fighter downed a Korean airliner that strayed into its airspace, killing everyone aboard and chilling relations.

beats.title: The Iran-Contra Affair Breaks
beats.description: News broke that arms sales to Iran had secretly funded rebels fighting a leftist government in Nicaragua.
beats.why_in: Cold War proxy war in Central America

beats.title: "Tear Down This Wall"
beats.description: At a divided city's famous gate, the US president called on the Soviet leader to open the barrier.

beats.title: Soviets Begin Leaving Afghanistan
beats.description: Under an agreement signed in Geneva, Soviet troops began leaving after nearly a decade of costly war.

beats.title: The Berlin Wall Falls
beats.description: Crowds streamed through the opened checkpoints and began tearing down the barrier that had split the city.

beats.title: Germany Reunifies
beats.description: East and West Germany merged into a single state, ending the division that symbolised the confrontation of the blocs.

beats.title: The Soviet Union Dissolves
beats.description: The red flag came down over the Kremlin as the superpower split into independent states, ending the Cold War.
